dedupe_keys.name: financial feasibility maps of solar irrigation under climate change in africa ifpri africa agriculture adaptation atlas

description: Maps of the internal rate of return (IRR) of solar-powered irrigation, and of its cost efficiency compared with diesel pumps, across Africa under 21 scenarios. The Dataverse record says the 126 maps were developed with support from the Africa Agriculture Adaptation Atlas, led by the Alliance of Bioversity International and CIAT and funded by the Gates Foundation. The files read cover six crops (chickpea, maize, onion, rice, tomato and wheat), a historical baseline and five climate models (ACCESS-ESM1-5, EC-Earth3, INM-CM5-0, MPI-ESM1-2-HR, MRI-ESM2-0) under SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5 for 2030 and 2050, as GeoTIFF IRR grids at an assumed 2.0 US dollars per watt-peak, JPEG maps, text summaries for solar and diesel, a land grid shapefile, an RWRAI table and a readme. Version 3.0 was released by IFPRI on 5 December 2025 and updated on 20 February 2026, free to download under custom terms set for this dataset. Coverage is Africa. Caveats: results depend on one panel price assumption and on crop water demand modelling, and the custom terms must be checked. For simulation it gives where solar irrigation pays off under climate change, to plan irrigation investment and reduce agriculture's dependence on diesel supply. A related catalogue record is the DLR global rooftop and cropland solar suitability maps.
